\chapter{Communication Complexity — Upper Bounds}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.UpperBounds
\section{Overview}

This module establishes elementary upper bounds on the deterministic communication
complexity of a two-party function $f : X \times Y \to \alpha$.  Each bound is witnessed
by an explicit protocol (Alice or Bob sends their raw input, and the other party replies
with the output) and is expressed in terms of the ceiling-logarithm $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$
of the relevant cardinality.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Complexity bounded by $\lceil\log|X|\rceil + \lceil\log|Y|\rceil$]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\difficulty{4}
For finite, nonempty types $X$ and $Y$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |X|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |Y|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Alice sends her entire input to Bob
and Bob then sends his entire input to Alice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complexity bounded by $\lceil\log|X|\rceil + \lceil\log|\alpha|\rceil$]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card_X_alpha}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card_X_alpha}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\difficulty{4}
For finite, nonempty types $X$ and $\alpha$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |X|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |\alpha|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Alice sends her input $x$ to Bob,
and Bob computes and sends back the output $f(x, y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complexity bounded by $\lceil\log|Y|\rceil + \lceil\log|\alpha|\rceil$]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card_Y_alpha}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_clog_card_Y_alpha}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\difficulty{4}
For finite, nonempty types $Y$ and $\alpha$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |Y|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |\alpha|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Bob sends his input $y$ to Alice,
and Alice computes and sends back the output $f(x, y)$.
\end{theorem}
